transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… the main thing is sleep. I haven’t been sleeping right. I lie there going over work stuff, arguments at home, and then I’m up around 3 or 4 and can’t really get back to sleep. I just start the day feeling like I didn’t rest at all. That’s what finally made me call the employee assistance program.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things?
I don’t know if I’d call it excessive. I mean… I think about things, probably too much sometimes, but it feels more like just normal stuff piling up.
Do you often feel tired or lacking in energy?
A little, I guess. Mostly I just feel worn out from not sleeping well. I still get through the day, but it’s… harder than it used to be.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s usually me going back over stuff I did wrong. Staying late at work, losing my temper in traffic, spending money on something stupid… and then I just keep thinking my wife and kids got stuck with someone who lets them down.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
No… I don’t think so. I get stressed, sure, but not like a sudden wave of fear that peaks or anything.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to relieve anxiety?
No… not really. I mean, I don’t think I have anything like that. I might double-check something once in a while, but not like I have to do it to calm down.
Do you have bad dreams or nightmares that wake you up?

Not nightmares, really. It’s more… I just don’t sleep right. I’ll lie there going over work stuff or arguments at home, then wake up around 3 or 4 and can’t really get back to sleep. I feel like I didn’t rest at all.
Do you have trouble focusing on things or making decisions?

Yeah… a bit. At work especially. I’ll be looking at a sales forecast or a client deck, and I end up reading the same slide over and over. Then I start second-guessing the numbers and can’t really decide what to say. It takes me way longer than it used to.
Do you feel tired or sluggish during the day, even when you've had a chance to rest?
I mean… I’m not sure. I get tired, yeah, but I don’t know if I’d call it sluggish exactly. Some days I’m just kind of worn down.
Do you think you worry more than most people about everyday things?
I don’t know… maybe not more than most people. I worry about the usual things, I guess, but I haven’t really compared it.
Do you think your worrying about work and home issues is something that most people would also worry about, or is it more than that for you?
I’m not really sure. I mean, work and home stuff… most people worry about that, right? I don’t know if mine is more than normal.
Do you think your worrying is controlling your life or interfering with your daily activities?

I wouldn’t say it’s controlling my life, exactly. I’m still getting to work and doing what I need to do… mostly. But yeah, there are gaps. My team’s had to cover for me when I’m not as prepared with forecasts or client stuff. And at home, I’m probably not as present with my wife and kids as I used to be.
Do you find that you're awake at the same time every night, like 3 or 4 am, even on weekends or days off when you don't have to wake up early?
Yeah… pretty much. I’ll wake up around 3 or 4 a lot, even if I don’t have to be up. Then I just lie there, thinking about work or stuff at home, and by morning it feels like I didn’t really sleep.
Is there something specific that happens right before you wake up at 3 or 4 am, or is it more of a consistent pattern regardless of what's going on?

It’s more of a pattern, I think. I don’t notice anything specific right before. I’ll just wake up around 3 or 4, and then I’m lying there replaying work stuff or arguments at home. That’s kind of what pushed me to call the employee assistance program… I’m just not sleeping right, and I start the day feeling like I didn’t really rest.
Is your waking up at 3 or 4 am related to something specific that's been stressing you out, or does it happen even when things are going smoothly?

It happens even when things are… fine, I guess. It’s not always one specific thing. I just wake up around 3 or 4 and start going over work stuff, or arguments at home, and then the day starts like I never really slept. That’s kind of why I called the employee assistance program.
Is there something in particular that's usually on your mind when you wake up at 3 or 4 am?

Mostly work stuff… and sometimes arguments at home. I just kind of lie there replaying it, and then it’s like the night’s over before it really feels like I slept. That’s part of why I ended up calling the employee assistance program.
Do you think the things that keep you awake at night, like work or arguments at home, are what's causing your sleep problems?

Yeah… I think they’re part of it. I wake up and start replaying work things or stuff from home, and then I can’t really settle back down. It got to the point where I felt like I wasn’t sleeping right at all, and that’s why I finally called the employee assistance program.
Do you think you would still wake up at 3 or 4 am if you weren't worrying about work and home issues?

I’m not sure. Maybe I’d still wake up some nights, but it’s usually when I start replaying work or an argument at home that I can’t get back to sleep. I just end up starting the day feeling like I didn’t really rest.
Do you think you would have trouble sleeping if you weren't worrying about work and home issues?

I don’t know for sure. I mean… the worrying is what keeps me up once I’m awake. I’ll wake around 3 or 4 and start replaying work or an argument at home, and then I don’t really feel like I rested. That’s what finally pushed me to call the employee assistance program.
